source: CK-12 Computer Science Concepts, Section 5.1, CC-BY-NC
notes: Class B document (13 units). Covers if/else logic with flowchart and traced example. One ECU for the worked example.

units.label: Hook: deciding what to wear (text)
units.content_summary: Every day you make conditional decisions: 'IF it's raining, THEN take an umbrella, ELSE wear sunglasses.' Programs make similar decisions using conditional statements.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: write a basic if statement; add an else clause; use comparison operators; trace program flow through a conditional.

units.label: if statement syntax (text)
units.content_summary: Basic syntax: `if (condition) { do this }`. The code inside the braces only runs if the condition evaluates to true. Example: `if (age >= 18) { print("Adult"); }`

units.label: if-else syntax (text)
units.content_summary: Adding else: `if (condition) { do this } else { do that }`. Exactly one branch executes. Example: `if (age >= 18) { print("Adult"); } else { print("Minor"); }`

units.label: Comparison operators table (image)
units.content_summary: Table listing comparison operators: == (equal), != (not equal), > (greater than), < (less than), >= (greater or equal), <= (less or equal), each with a short example.

units.label: Flowchart of if-else logic (image)
units.content_summary: Flowchart showing: START → decision diamond (condition?) → Yes branch and No branch → both merge → END. Standard if-else visual representation.

units.label: Worked example: age checker (text)
units.content_summary: Full code: `int age = 15; if (age >= 18) { print("Adult"); } else { print("Minor"); }`. Trace: age=15, condition (15>=18) is false, else branch runs, prints "Minor".

units.label: Worked example trace diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Step-by-step trace diagram showing the age checker code execution: variable assignment, condition evaluation (false), branch taken (else), output produced.

units.label: else if for multiple conditions (text)
units.content_summary: For more than two outcomes, use else if: `if (score>=90) {A} else if (score>=80) {B} else {C}`. Conditions checked in order; first true one runs, rest are skipped.

units.label: Video: conditionals in a game (video)
units.content_summary: Video showing a simple game where conditional statements determine outcomes (win/lose/tie) based on player input, with the corresponding code shown alongside the running game.

units.label: Practice problems (text)
units.content_summary: Four problems: write an if statement for a given scenario; trace a conditional program with given inputs; convert a described decision into if-else code; identify the bug in a given conditional.
